This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Taipei Songshan Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Taipei Songshan Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/tw/taipei/RCSS.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather prediction models from agencies including the China Meteorological Administration point to a daily maximum near 30°C in Qingdao on August 11 under partly cloudy skies with isolated showers possible. Trader consensus, reflected in the closely matched 34.5% implied probability for 30°C and 28.5% for 31°C, centers on this range because coastal marine influence and typical August humidity limit extreme heating, while any afternoon convection could cap the peak below 32°C. Ensemble spreads show modest uncertainty around timing and intensity of precipitation, which explains the secondary support for 29°C and 32°C. Historical climatology places the August average high near 28–30°C, providing context for why probabilities decay sharply outside the 29–31°C band ahead of final observational data.

Reduced monsoon cloud cover and convective activity allow greater solar insolation and less evaporative cooling, nudging daytime maxima toward the upper end of the late-monsoon climatological range of 31–33°C. Persistent high humidity and a moderating Arabian Sea breeze typically cap extremes, while ensemble model spreads and any residual low-level moisture convergence introduce the narrow uncertainty separating 32°C from 33°C. eventMetadata.context_description: The closely matched odds favoring 30°C and 31°C as Manila's highest temperature on August 11 stem from typical late-summer monsoon variability, where official forecasts from PAGASA and global models show afternoon peaks hovering near those thresholds amid high humidity and frequent cloud cover. Daily maximums in the Philippine capital during August average around 31°C but often shift by 1–2°C depending on rainfall timing, wind patterns from the southwest monsoon, and the urban heat island effect that amplifies readings at official stations. Traders are weighting the 35°C bin highest because most operational runs cluster the maximum in that narrow window, with modest downside risk to 34°C if cloud cover or a slightly faster trough arrival occurs. Upside to 37°C or above remains limited unless models trend warmer in the final 48-hour updates. Historical August climatology (typical highs near 25°C) underscores how anomalous the current pattern is, but resolution hinges on the official Météo-France observed maximum, which will be finalized shortly after the date.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on the 32–33°C range for Karachi’s peak temperature on August 12 reflects short-term forecast uncertainty typical of the southwest monsoon, when afternoon convection, variable cloud cover, and sea-breeze timing can shift maxima by 1–2°C. Latest global model ensembles show a tight spread around these values, with 33°C slightly favored by drier boundary-layer conditions and stronger solar heating if monsoon breaks occur. Key variables include the strength and timing of any embedded low-pressure systems, soil moisture from recent rains, and urban heat-island effects, all of which remain sensitive to the next 48-hour model updates from agencies such as the Pakistan Meteorological Department. Historical August climatology places average highs near 32°C, underscoring why small shifts in moisture or wind keep the two leading outcomes nearly tied.
